selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: /srv/data, datauser, and node1 filesystem state before changes
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing datauser or /srv/data, ext4 root with no quota support, xfsprogs already installed

selected_evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself
selected_evidence.summary: Created datauser, built dedicated XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, set bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota, and demonstrated kernel-level enforcement: 60MB write succeeded, 150MB write was hard-blocked by XFS with 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly 100MB used, then cleaned up leaving quota at 0/100M

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline capture on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, active /srv/data mount, quota config (datauser 0/100M), fstab entry, and datauser account presence prior to restart
Issued native 'shutdown -r now'; command acknowledgement returned (stream closed) before the node disconnected, confirming the restart was triggered

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart polling and availability recovery
selected_evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down/rebooting), second poll succeeded with a fresh uptime, confirming exec access returned after restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 973e294e-ea59-4f62-8a8a-a60c5071b1c2 differs from pre-restart value, proving a genuine reboot occurred. Verified /srv/data fstab mount, datauser account, and XFS quota (Enforcement: ON, 100M soft/hard) all recovered automatically, and re-ran the 150MB write test which was again blocked at exactly 100MB by the filesystem, confirming enforcement survives restart

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail

echo "== STEP 1: create datauser =="
sudo -n useradd -m -s /usr/sbin/nologin datauser
id datauser

echo "== STEP 2: create backing image for dedicated XFS filesystem =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /var/lib/srv-data-backing
sudo -n fallocate -l 512M /var/lib/srv-data-backing/data.img
sudo -n mkfs.xfs -q /var/lib/srv-data-backing/data.img

echo "== STEP 3: mountpoint + fstab entry (persist across reboot) =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /srv/data
grep -q '/srv/data' /etc/fstab || \
  echo '/var/lib/srv-data-backing/data.img /srv/data xfs loop,usrquota,prjquota,defaults 0 0' | sudo -n tee -a /etc/fstab

echo "== STEP 4: mount =="
sudo -n mount /srv/data
mount | grep /srv/data

echo "== STEP 5: permissions =="
sudo -n chmod 1777 /srv/data

echo "== STEP 6: set 100MB user quota (soft=hard) for datauser, kernel-enforced by XFS =="
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'limit -u bsoft=100m bhard=100m datauser' /srv/data

echo "== STEP 7: verify quota config =="
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'state -u' /srv/data

echo "== STEP 8: functional test as datauser - write under limit (60MB) should succeed =="
sudo -n -u datauser dd if=/dev/zero of=/srv/data/ok.bin bs=1M count=60 status=none
ls -la /srv/data/ok.bin
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data

echo "== STEP 9: write over limit (150MB) should be blocked by filesystem quota =="
set +e
sudo -n -u datauser dd if=/dev/zero of=/srv/data/over.bin bs=1M count=150 status=none
RC=$?
set -e
echo "dd exit code (expect nonzero due to EDQUOT/ENOSPC): $RC"
ls -la /srv/data/
du -sh /srv/data/over.bin 2>/dev/null || true
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data

echo "== STEP 10: cleanup test files, keep quota config =="
sudo -n rm -f /srv/data/ok.bin /srv/data/over.bin
sudo -n xfs_quota -x -c 'report -u -h' /srv/data
echo "DONE"
